exposure: compliance with evidence-based audit criteria for cesarean section
outcome: proportion of nonmedically indicated cesarean sections
cohort: Women who underwent cesarean section at five high-volume urban maternity units in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, between October 2021 and August 2022.
finding: Approximately two in five (39.7%) cesarean sections performed in the studied units were categorized as nonmedically indicated based on pre-defined audit criteria.
mod_finding: Two in five cesarean sections were categorized as nonmedically indicated due to reasons such as one previous cesarean section without a trial of labor, reported prolonged labor without actual slow progress, and fetal distress with a normal fetal heart rate.
cross-section timing: Data was collected retrospectively from October 1st, 2021 to August 31st, 2022, focusing on 3-month periods within this timeframe at each maternity unit.
